parsed.explanation: The objection identifies a genuine gap. Because each selected F_k is disjoint from the current label {x_1,...,x_k}, a prime c occurring in infinitely many F_k cannot already lie on the actual infinite branch. “Insert c” therefore passes to a different branch. The subsequent selected sets on that branch need not equal the original F_k, since F_D was chosen separately for each node; thus “until the next occurrence nothing changes” is unjustified. Redundancy on this modified path also does not imply that any node of the original infinite branch would be contracted. No other part of the write-up proves that the pruned tree, or the family of minimal finite transversals, is finite. Since that finiteness supplies the finite list B_1,...,B_s and hence the modulus L, the lower_bound obligation and the proof remain incomplete.
